artworks.title: Hermes Stealing the Cattle of Apollo (Brygos Painter cup)
artworks.description: Attic red-figure (Vatican): newborn Hermes drives off Apollo's cattle — the Homeric Hymn theft painted for a drinking party.

artworks.title: Young Mercury Stealing Cattle from Apollo's Herd
artworks.description: Rijksmuseum panel: the child Mercury leading Apollo's herd — the Hymn's dawn cattle-raid restaged as Dutch cabinet myth.

artworks.title: Mercury Stealing the Cattle of the Gods
artworks.description: Poynter's Walker Art Gallery canvas: Mercury as cattle-thief among the herd — Victorian Academic reading of the infant god's first crime.

artworks.title: Mercury Inventing the Lyre
artworks.description: Yale Center print: Mercury fashions the tortoise-shell lyre — the Hymn's other dawn invention, the bargain that will buy Apollo's forgiveness.

popCulture.title: Homeric Hymns
popCulture.description: The Hymn to Hermes — the newborn cattle-thief who invents the lyre — remains the classic birth-song of the trickster god.

popCulture.title: Hermes
popCulture.description: Born at dawn, thief by noon — Hermes' infancy is still the template for divine cunning in Western myth.
